findings.what: SQL server has publicNetworkAccess Enabled plus the AllowAzureServices 0.0.0.0 rule, so any Azure-hosted caller can reach port 1433.
findings.why: Network exposure hardening. Entra-only auth and TLS 1.2 limit the risk, so it is not exploitable on its own. A private endpoint or the app's outbound IPs would shrink the surface. The 'evidence only, never deployed' scope makes this non-blocking.

findings.what: Basic-auth publishing credentials for SCM/Kudu (and FTP) are not disabled; only ftpsState is Disabled.
findings.why: Least privilege and misconfiguration. The pipeline deploys with az webapp deploy through the service connection and doesn't need basic auth. Add basicPublishingCredentialsPolicies for scm and ftp with allow=false.

findings.what: The deployment service principal is a member of the SQL admin group and runs migrations and user grants as admin, in every environment including prod.
findings.why: Least privilege. The app's own identity is correctly limited to db_datareader and db_datawriter, so it holds no DDL rights. The pipeline identity is a standing SQL admin, and the design should record that as an accepted trade-off.

findings.what: dotnet-ef is installed as a global tool with no version pin, and the agent image is ubuntu-latest, so a floating tool version runs in the build that produces the prod migration script.
findings.why: Pipeline supply-chain hygiene. Pin the tool version (--version, or a tool manifest) so the packages are reproducible and approved.

API3, API4, API6 and API9 are marked covered because the diff is infrastructure/** only. It changes no DTOs, rate limits, refund flows or routes, so these checks are vacuously met.

Secrets: none found. The SQL admin is Entra-only (azureADOnlyAuthentication true, no administratorLogin or password). The app connection string uses 'Authentication=Active Directory Managed Identity' with no credentials. The App Insights connection string is an ingestion endpoint, not a credential. The three param files hold all-zero placeholder GUIDs and the real values come from a variable group. A grep of infrastructure/ for Password=, AccountKey, SharedAccessKey, sig=, tokens, local paths and emails found nothing.

Identity, TLS and exposure items that are met: system-assigned identity on the app; SQL minimalTlsVersion 1.2; app httpsOnly true, minTlsVersion 1.2, ftpsState Disabled; ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production, which keeps OpenAPI and Scalar off; health check path set.

Pipeline: pr is none, so PR builds can't reach service connections. Prod approval lives on the 'policies-prod' Azure DevOps environment, outside the repo, and the checker only verifies the environment name. The what-if runs before create. The only variable group is policies-<env>, and the pipeline sets no secret values. No third-party tasks beyond Microsoft UseDotNet@2 and AzureCLI@2.

Dynamic input: the inline sqlcmd -Q interpolates $(appName), a Bicep deployment output derived from the fixed name 'app-policies-<env>'. It is not attacker-controlled and the user is created idempotently.

API8 deployment nuance, not a diff defect: httpsOnly on App Service redirects HTTP at the platform front end, so the app's 400 /problems/https-required path is never reached. App Service Linux may also set ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED on its own, which the API4 rate-limit design says never to rely on. Check the README or deployment notes for that interaction. Neither point is introduced by this diff.
Not present, as hardening candidates only: SQL auditing and Defender for SQL, Log Analytics and SQL diagnostic settings, and a private network path.

Not security, but flagged for the reviewer: az deployment --parameters accepts a .bicepparam file combined with inline key=value overrides only on newer az CLI versions. The gates never ran az, so this is untested.

NET extras: no .cs in the diff, so raw SQL, decimal money, logging and package checks have nothing to inspect. gate.vulnerable reports 8 projects with no vulnerable packages. The Python checker needs PyYAML and jsonschema, which it doesn't pin or declare anywhere in the repo. That is dev tooling only, not shipped.
